#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A missing ELF must fail in the driver with a clear "ELF not found", BEFORE any
# engine is launched -- never the cryptic downstream
# "qemu-system-riscv64: Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS ...".
# Covers fast (the reported case) + cycle; hybrid already guarded (regression).
# The fix lives at the one shared resolver (abs_elf), so fast/cycle/cycle-gdb
# all inherit it; this test pins fast + cycle + hybrid.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "need build/andesim"

MISSING="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/__definitely_absent__.elf"
[ -e "$MISSING" ] && fail "test bug: $MISSING unexpectedly exists"

# assert_missing <label> <args...>: run the driver, require a non-zero exit, the
# driver's own "ELF not found" diagnostic, and the ABSENCE of any engine spawn
# ("Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS" proves qemu was reached -- it must not be).
assert_missing() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "$label: missing ELF should exit non-zero, got 0: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'ELF not found' \
    || fail "$label: missing the 'ELF not found' diagnostic: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS' \
    && fail "$label: reached qemu instead of failing in the driver: $out"
  ok "$label: missing ELF -> clean 'ELF not found', no engine spawn"
}

# fast: the reported bug -- must not hand the missing path to qemu.
assert_missing "fast" run --mode fast "$MISSING"

# cycle: reaches the shared resolver only after engine discovery + selection, so
# it needs a concrete --engine (and VSIM_BIN_DIR for discovery). The existence
# check is arch-independent -- elf_xlen of a missing file is 0, so no arch
# mismatch fires first regardless of which engine we pick.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
export VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR"
eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$eng" ]; then
  assert_missing "cycle" run --mode cycle --engine "$eng" "$MISSING"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle: no vsim engine discoverable under $BINDIR"
fi

# hybrid: already validates existence up front -- regression guard.
assert_missing "hybrid" run --mode hybrid "$MISSING"

# hybrid trigger/pc gating: --mode hybrid REQUIRES --trigger (marker|pc), and
# --trigger pc REQUIRES both --pc-start and --pc-end (a symbol name or 0x
# address, resolved against the ELF .symtab). There is no silent marker
# default -- an unmarked ELF run without a trigger used to fast-forward the

#
#   1. hybrid, no --trigger                  -> usage error (rc 2)
#   2. hybrid --trigger pc, no --pc-*        -> usage error (rc 2)
#   3. hybrid --trigger pc, only --pc-start  -> usage error (rc 2)
#   4. hybrid --trigger pc, unreadable ELF   -> resolve error surfaces (rc 2)
#   5. hybrid --trigger bogus                -> unknown trigger (rc 2)
set -uo pipefail

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

ELF="${ELF:-/no/such/file.elf}"  # a symbol boundary forces resolve_pc to read it

  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"

# F8 contract: `run --mode cycle` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'

fi
EOF
